newsitem.title: FRANCE: Franco-Cuban sugar barter talks start next week.
newsitem.headline: Franco-Cuban sugar barter talks start next week.

text.p: French and Cuban government officials will meet next week in Paris to discuss the renewal of a food-for-sugar barter deal, French banking sources said on Wednesday.
A delegation of Cuban officials was expected between January 20 and January 24 for meetings with representatives of the French finance ministry, they said.
There was no immediate confirmation from the French finance ministry.
The seven-year-old deal, guaranteed by a Coface export credit, is traditionally renewed at this time of the year.
Last year's agreement, worth $155 million, involved the supply to Cuba of food products, mostly wheat. In return Cuba supplied French traders with sugar for sale on the world market.
Banking sources said the value of the barter deal for 1997 might be around or slightly higher than $155 million.
One banker cited a figure of $175 million.
Farm products, mostly wheat but also milk products and farm equipment parts, were expected to be included in the deal.
France has become the leading exporter of soft wheat to Cuba, followed by Canada, because of a 36-year-old U.S. embargo against Cuba.
France sold close to 500,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Cuba in the 1995/96 (July/June) season and 800,000 tonnes in 1994/95, statistics from France's grain office ONIC showed.
The International Grains Council expects Cuba to import 900,000 tonnes of wheat and flour including durum wheat and semolina from world markets in 1996/97.
